author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Seattle Seahawks erased a 10-point deficit and defeated the New England Patriots 13-10 Wednesday night in a rematch of last season’s Super Bowl.

Seattle backup quarterback Drew Lock entered after starter Sam Darnold injured his hip on the opening drive. The Seahawks managed only a field goal through three quarters before Lock connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 45-yard touchdown on fourth-and-1.

Three fourth-quarter interceptions by Seattle’s defense turned the game. Nehemiah Pritchett and Julian Love picked off Drake Maye to set up the comeback and go-ahead field goal. Josh Jobe then made a toe-tapping interception in the end zone during New England’s final drive to preserve the win.

Maye threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to rookie Eli Raridon in the first half, and Andy Borregales added a 50-yard field goal. Patriots receiver A.J. Brown left with a right-ankle injury. New England returns home to face Pittsburgh on September 20.
dek: Seattle’s backup quarterback led two late scoring drives while New England threw three fourth-quarter interceptions in a 13-10 loss.
headline: Seahawks rally past Patriots 13-10 in Super Bowl rematch
